pathway.title: ATS Corp /ATS — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The strongest support is liquidity and visibility. Cash of CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn on the CAD 900.0 million committed revolver sit against near-term debt maturities of only CAD 2.4 million of bank indebtedness and a negligible current portion of long-term debt. Backlog of CAD 2,009 million, with 61.62% of it in life sciences, and second-quarter bookings that rose 12.7% give revenue visibility into fiscal 2027, although management guides third-quarter revenue to CAD 640 million to CAD 680 million, below the CAD 760.7 million of a year earlier. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 31

The weakest dimension is margin stability. Second-quarter revenue fell 8.6% but adjusted EBITDA fell 22.2%, and the adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 12.1% from 14.2%, so fixed costs are not flexing with volume. Reported EBITDA is lower again: CAD 277.8 million over the last twelve months against CAD 381.1 million adjusted, because CAD 103.3 million of add-backs, CAD 99.8 million of it restructuring or reorganisation cost, is excluded from the adjusted measure. Creditors should underwrite reported earnings until the program's savings are visible. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C5

Net debt excluding leases is 3.76x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA against 2.75x at fiscal 2026 year end, or 3.51x pro forma for the sale of two U.S. facilities, which was completed after the quarter end on a day the filings do not state. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 3.05x, down from 3.72x. On the company's own definition, which includes leases and pro forma EBITDA, leverage of 3.1x sits above its target range of 2.0x to 3.0x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 11

Cash flow is less durable than its conversion suggests. Free cash flow was CAD 258.6 million over the last twelve months and CAD 36.5 million in the first half of fiscal 2027, equal to 0.93x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, but fiscal 2026 included a CAD 246.6 million working capital release and the first half of fiscal 2026 included an EV settlement collection. Contract liabilities, the customer advances that fund projects, fell to CAD 290.8 million from CAD 307.3 million at year end, so slower bookings would draw on cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 18; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 20–21

Refinancing is a question for the next two years, not an immediate one. The US dollar notes of USD 350.0 million, CAD 494.9 million at the period-end rate, mature on 15 December 2028 and the credit facility, with CAD 190.0 million drawn, on 4 December 2029, so access on acceptable terms depends on leverage returning to the 2.0x to 3.0x range. The senior notes' security and ranking and the covenant tests are not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6

Financial policy is the swing factor. The company repaid debt in fiscal 2026 but bought back CAD 61.3 million of shares in the second quarter with leverage above target, has an interim finance chief and reports an unremediated control weakness. No sponsor or controlling owner is identified, so the board and management alone decide whether cash goes to creditors or shareholders, and restricted payment limits are not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 2

runs.text: Strength one is liquidity. Cash of CAD 231.0 million and an undrawn committed revolver of CAD 860.0 million, with only CAD 2.4 million of near-term bank debt, mean the company can fund restructuring and working capital from available resources, which lowers the chance that earnings weakness becomes a liquidity event before the December 2028 notes. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 24–28

Strength two is the order book. Backlog of CAD 2,009 million, led by life sciences at 61.62%, and a trailing book-to-bill of about 1.05 times give partial coverage of revenue while non-life-sciences orders recover, which supports cash generation through the guided third quarter. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 15; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6

Strength three is a self-help program with funding. Annualised savings of CAD 65 million to CAD 75 million, about 250 basis points of margin, and CAD 71.2 million from the facility sale, which management intends to use for restructuring, address the fixed-cost base that is currently amplifying revenue declines. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength four is a deleveraging record and a longer runway. The company's leverage measure fell to 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end from 3.9x and the credit facility was extended to December 2029, which reduces refinancing pressure and shows past willingness to repay debt. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength five is service content. Services were 26.90% of second-quarter revenue and management expects recurring revenue of 25% to 35%, which stabilises cash flow through the capital cycle if the share rises. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 9

Weakness one is operating leverage. Revenue fell 8.6% and adjusted EBITDA 22.2% in the second quarter, so a further volume shortfall cuts earnings faster than revenue and pushes leverage and interest cover toward weaker levels. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness two is dependence on add-backs. The CAD 103.3 million gap between adjusted and reported EBITDA is 27.11% of adjusted EBITDA, so the company's own leverage of 3.1x understates the cash cost of its program for as long as charges recur. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5

Weakness three is financial policy while leverage is above target. The CAD 61.3 million of repurchases in the second quarter used cash that could have reduced net debt, and the filings give no restricted payment limit that would stop repeat repurchases. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6

Weakness four is reporting reliability. An unremediated material weakness in internal control, an interim finance chief and a new chief executive raise the chance that adjusted measures or accruals are later revised. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38

Weakness five is cash flow volatility. Free cash flow moved from a CAD 52.3 million outflow in fiscal 2025 to an inflow of CAD 371.7 million in fiscal 2026 as the company states it, on working capital and a settlement, and the first half of fiscal 2027 produced only CAD 36.5 million, so debt service cannot be assumed from a single year's figure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 18

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The supplied filings report no new bond issue after December 2024; recent debt activity is the extension of the secured credit facility and use of the revolver. On 4 December 2025 the company amended the facility, moving maturity to 4 December 2029 and setting a CAD 900.0 million committed revolver and a fully drawn CAD 150.0 million term facility, with CAD 2.6 million of costs deferred and amortised. The notes outstanding are US dollar notes of USD 350.0 million due 15 December 2028 and Canadian dollar notes of CAD 600.0 million due 21 August 2032, the latter placed in two steps on 21 August 2024 and 19 December 2024, the second at a premium of CAD 1.3 million. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 20; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28

Other transactions bear on creditors. After 27 September 2026 the company completed the sale of two U.S. facilities for CAD 71.2 million, with an estimated gain of about CAD 12.2 million to be recognised in the third quarter of fiscal 2027 and an agreement to lease one facility back; a German facility remains held for sale. The transportation reorganization announced in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was completed in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, and the Fixed Cost Transformation Program, announced on 6 August 2026 with a European footprint consolidation as its first phase, is in progress. Heidolph and Paxiom were acquired before fiscal 2026, with about CAD 179 million of cash acquisitions printed for fiscal 2025 and none since. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-06-28_ats-pressreleasexfy27q1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 18; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 4

fields.value: Net leverage on reported EBITDA has risen to 3.76x over the last twelve months to 27 September 2026 from 2.75x at fiscal 2026 year end, and interest cover has fallen to 3.05x from 3.72x, so creditors now depend on liquidity more than on earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is ample, with cash of CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn on the committed revolver, and the first large principal maturity is the US dollar notes due in December 2028. The company's own 3.1x leverage relies on add-backs of CAD 103.3 million over the same twelve months, almost all restructuring and reorganisation costs, which must stop recurring for the adjusted view to hold. Covenant levels and the audited annual notes are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established.

fields.value: Reported-basis leverage is the figure to anchor on. Net debt excluding leases was 3.76x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 27 September 2026, against 2.75x at fiscal 2026 year end, because reported EBITDA over the last twelve months fell to CAD 277.8 million from CAD 362.7 million while total debt barely moved. Net debt rose by about CAD 49 million, mostly because cash fell by about CAD 54 million after CAD 61.3 million of share repurchases in the second quarter, and the company itself says the repurchases added about 0.1x to its leverage. Cash interest cover on the same basis fell to 3.05x from 3.72x. The cause is earnings, not borrowing: first-half revenue fell 7.21% and adjusted EBITDA fell 15.54%, so a further decline would erode cover faster than debt can be repaid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company's headline looks steadier because it adds costs back. On adjusted EBITDA, net leverage excluding leases is 2.74x against 2.41x at year end, and the company's own 3.1x, which includes lease liabilities and its pro forma EBITDA, compares with 2.8x at year end and sits above its target range of 2.0x to 3.0x. The CAD 103.3 million gap between adjusted and reported EBITDA is 27.11% of adjusted EBITDA, and CAD 99.8 million of it is restructuring or reorganisation cost that management expects to continue for about 15 more months under the Fixed Cost Transformation Program. Until those costs stop, adjusted leverage understates the cash the business consumes.

fields.value: Liquidity is not the constraint today. At 27 September 2026 the company held CAD 231.0 million of cash and had CAD 860.0 million undrawn on its CAD 900.0 million committed revolver, which matures in December 2029; it also states CAD 277.2 million more is available under letter of credit facilities, while CAD 274.4 million of letters of credit are outstanding. The next principal maturities are the US dollar notes in December 2028, CAD 494.9 million at the period-end rate, and the credit facility in December 2029, with CAD 190.0 million drawn, so refinancing is a task for fiscal 2029 and 2030 rather than now. The risk is access: the revolver sits under a net debt to EBITDA test and an interest coverage test whose levels are not supplied, so rising leverage could narrow what can be drawn before it narrows cash.

fields.value: Cash flow over the last twelve months is weaker than fiscal 2026 suggests. Free cash flow from the statements was about CAD 259 million over the last twelve months and about CAD 37 million in the first half of fiscal 2027, against about CAD 372 million in fiscal 2026, which included a CAD 246.6 million release of working capital, and about CAD 150 million in the first half of fiscal 2026, which included collection of an EV customer settlement whose amount is not stated. Free cash flow was 0.93x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, which is solid only because reported EBITDA is itself low.

fields.value: The working capital cushion is thinning. Non-cash working capital rose to 13.4% of annualised adjusted revenue from 12.1% at year end, and contract liabilities, the customer advances that fund projects, fell to CAD 290.8 million from CAD 307.3 million at year end and CAD 330.1 million at the prior year end. These advances are secured partly by letters of credit within the CAD 274.4 million outstanding, so if bookings slow the float unwinds and consumes cash while the letter of credit lines stay in use; the split of letters of credit by purpose is not stated. Provisions rose by CAD 6.7 million as restructuring costs were recognised ahead of payment, so a cash outflow is still to come.

fields.value: ATS Corp /ATS (ats), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: business, transaction, ownership and governance facts from the supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ATS is a publicly listed automation builder with no sponsor or controlling owner identified in the filings, so creditors depend on management's financial policy, which is in transition: a new chief executive, an interim finance chief, an unremediated control weakness and a restructuring program.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand is mixed: second-quarter bookings of CAD 827 million rose 12.7% year on year but revenue fell 8.6%, and management no longer expects its fiscal 2027 goals of modest revenue growth and margin expansion. The company spent CAD 61.3 million on share repurchases in the quarter while its own leverage measure sat above its target range, and the sale of two U.S. facilities for CAD 71.2 million is meant to fund restructuring. Ownership percentages, guarantor entities and sponsor economics are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ATS builds and services automated manufacturing systems, and its revenue is project-driven with a growing service share. Of fiscal 2026 adjusted revenue of CAD 2,970.1 million, construction contracts were 53.84%, services 24.37% and goods 21.78%, and life sciences was 51.24% by market and North America 52.48% by customer location. Services were 26.90% of second-quarter revenue and management expects recurring revenue of 25% to 35% on a trailing basis, which matters because service revenue is described as margin-accretive and less tied to customer capital cycles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand has softened outside life sciences. Order backlog of CAD 2,009 million is 2.9% below a year earlier, and 61.62% of it is life sciences at CAD 1,238 million, while industrial and consumer backlog fell to CAD 312 million from CAD 431 million. Management attributes weaker non-life-sciences orders to timing and to tariffs that took effect in late August 2026 and were modified at the end of October to remove the effect on most covered products, and it guides third-quarter revenue to CAD 640 million to CAD 680 million against CAD 760.7 million a year earlier. Revenue therefore steps down before bookings can recover, so cash and leverage, not backlog, are the near-term constraint for creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leadership and controls are in transition. The chief executive joined on 12 January 2026 and the chief financial officer's resignation took effect on 15 February 2026, since when the corporate controller has acted as interim finance chief. The company states that its disclosure controls were not effective at 27 September 2026 because of a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting first reported in fiscal 2026, and an ERP upgrade that went live in the quarter is still stabilising. For creditors the risk is the reliability of reported figures and of add-back classification while earnings fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is partly creditor-aligned and partly not. The company brought its net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA measure down to 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end from 3.9x a year earlier and extended its credit facility to 4 December 2029, but in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 it bought back CAD 61.3 million of shares at an average of CAD 27.32 per share while the same measure was 3.1x against a stated target range of 2.0x to 3.0x. Management says it expects to stay moderately above the range through fiscal 2027 and will pursue such uses only where there is a clear path back to range. The filings do not disclose the restricted payment limits that would cap further repurchases, so capacity cannot be separated from willingness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Restructuring is now continuous and sizeable. The Fixed Cost Transformation Program announced on 6 August 2026 targets annualised savings of CAD 65 million to CAD 75 million, about 250 basis points of margin and half of the 500 basis points still needed to reach the 15% long-term margin target. Implementation is expected to run about 15 more months with workforce reductions of several hundred including subcontractors, and CAD 21.3 million of restructuring was charged in the second quarter against nil a year earlier. The charges are added back to adjusted measures but are cash costs, and the sale of two U.S. facilities for CAD 71.2 million after the quarter end is intended to fund them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings name no sponsor, controlling shareholder or ownership percentage, so neither sponsor support nor sponsor extraction can be evidenced; the shares are listed on the TSX and NYSE and the audit committee has three independent directors. The debt was shaped by two placements of Canadian dollar notes due 2032 in 2024, US dollar notes due 2028 and a secured credit facility extended in December 2025, and guarantees come from subsidiaries that are borrowers or guarantors under the credit facility, whose names are not listed. Overall, ATS presents medium governance risk for creditors: the key supported behavior is share repurchases above the leverage target during a restructuring, which matters because it uses liquidity ahead of an earnings recovery, and the countervailing evidence is the fiscal 2026 deleveraging and the extended facility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against caution is operational and financial. Bookings rose 12.7% in the second quarter, life sciences backlog ended the quarter at the highest level in the company's history, the end-of-October change to tariffs removes the effect on most covered products, and the company states CAD 966.7 million of unutilised credit alongside a leverage measure that was 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end. Management also expects restructuring payback in under one year. This view would win if revenue stays inside the guided third-quarter range and non-life-sciences bookings convert, which would let earnings recover without further share repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A more positive view would follow leverage returning inside 2.0x to 3.0x, no further repurchases until it does, remediation of the control weakness and restructuring charges ending on the stated timetable. A more negative view would follow third-quarter revenue below CAD 640 million, a further bookings delay outside life sciences, repurchases or acquisitions while the measure exceeds 3.0x, or covenant levels that prove tight once disclosed.

fields.value: The supplied filings report no new bond issue after December 2024; recent debt activity is the extension of the secured credit facility and use of the revolver. On 4 December 2025 the company amended the facility, moving maturity to 4 December 2029 and setting a CAD 900.0 million committed revolver and a fully drawn CAD 150.0 million term facility, with CAD 2.6 million of costs deferred and amortised. The notes outstanding are US dollar notes of USD 350.0 million due 15 December 2028 and Canadian dollar notes of CAD 600.0 million due 21 August 2032, the latter placed in two steps on 21 August 2024 and 19 December 2024, the second at a premium of CAD 1.3 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions bear on creditors. After 27 September 2026 the company completed the sale of two U.S. facilities for CAD 71.2 million, with an estimated gain of about CAD 12.2 million to be recognised in the third quarter of fiscal 2027 and an agreement to lease one facility back; a German facility remains held for sale. The transportation reorganization announced in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was completed in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, and the Fixed Cost Transformation Program, announced on 6 August 2026 with a European footprint consolidation as its first phase, is in progress. Heidolph and Paxiom were acquired before fiscal 2026, with about CAD 179 million of cash acquisitions printed for fiscal 2025 and none since.

Countervailing evidence is the fiscal 2026 deleveraging and the extended credit facility.

fields.value: Liquidity is the strongest support, with cash of CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn on the committed revolver, and no large principal falls due before December 2028. The weakest dimension is margin stability: the second-quarter revenue decline of 8.6% produced a 22.2% fall in adjusted EBITDA, and CAD 103.3 million of last-twelve-months add-backs separate reported from adjusted EBITDA. The sale of two U.S. facilities was completed after 27 September 2026 on a day the filings do not state. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is not established.

fields.value: The strongest support is liquidity and visibility. Cash of CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn on the CAD 900.0 million committed revolver sit against near-term debt maturities of only CAD 2.4 million of bank indebtedness and a negligible current portion of long-term debt. Backlog of CAD 2,009 million, with 61.62% of it in life sciences, and second-quarter bookings that rose 12.7% give revenue visibility into fiscal 2027, although management guides third-quarter revenue to CAD 640 million to CAD 680 million, below the CAD 760.7 million of a year earlier.

fields.value: The weakest dimension is margin stability. Second-quarter revenue fell 8.6% but adjusted EBITDA fell 22.2%, and the adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 12.1% from 14.2%, so fixed costs are not flexing with volume. Reported EBITDA is lower again: CAD 277.8 million over the last twelve months against CAD 381.1 million adjusted, because CAD 103.3 million of add-backs, CAD 99.8 million of it restructuring or reorganisation cost, is excluded from the adjusted measure. Creditors should underwrite reported earnings until the program's savings are visible.

Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 3.05x, down from 3.72x. On the company's own definition, which includes leases and pro forma EBITDA, leverage of 3.1x sits above its target range of 2.0x to 3.0x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is less durable than its conversion suggests. Free cash flow was CAD 258.6 million over the last twelve months and CAD 36.5 million in the first half of fiscal 2027, equal to 0.93x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, but fiscal 2026 included a CAD 246.6 million working capital release and the first half of fiscal 2026 included an EV settlement collection. Contract liabilities, the customer advances that fund projects, fell to CAD 290.8 million from CAD 307.3 million at year end, so slower bookings would draw on cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing is a question for the next two years, not an immediate one. The US dollar notes of USD 350.0 million, CAD 494.9 million at the period-end rate, mature on 15 December 2028 and the credit facility, with CAD 190.0 million drawn, on 4 December 2029, so access on acceptable terms depends on leverage returning to the 2.0x to 3.0x range. The senior notes' security and ranking and the covenant tests are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the swing factor. The company repaid debt in fiscal 2026 but bought back CAD 61.3 million of shares in the second quarter with leverage above target, has an interim finance chief and reports an unremediated control weakness. No sponsor or controlling owner is identified, so the board and management alone decide whether cash goes to creditors or shareholders, and restricted payment limits are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that life sciences backlog and bookings are rising while tariffs have been eased, the company states CAD 966.7 million of unutilised credit, its own leverage measure was 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end, and management expects restructuring to pay back within a year. This view would win if third-quarter revenue lands inside the guided range, the adjusted EBITDA margin recovers toward the 13.3% of the first quarter, and the facility sale proceeds fund restructuring so that net leverage returns to its target range without new repurchases.

fields.value: The downside illustration applies the first-half fall in adjusted EBITDA to last-twelve-months reported EBITDA as an analyst assumption; it is not a forecast and leaves out savings, working capital and interest changes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength one is liquidity. Cash of CAD 231.0 million and an undrawn committed revolver of CAD 860.0 million, with only CAD 2.4 million of near-term bank debt, mean the company can fund restructuring and working capital from available resources, which lowers the chance that earnings weakness becomes a liquidity event before the December 2028 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength two is the order book. Backlog of CAD 2,009 million, led by life sciences at 61.62%, and a trailing book-to-bill of about 1.05 times give partial coverage of revenue while non-life-sciences orders recover, which supports cash generation through the guided third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 15; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength three is a self-help program with funding. Annualised savings of CAD 65 million to CAD 75 million, about 250 basis points of margin, and CAD 71.2 million from the facility sale, which management intends to use for restructuring, address the fixed-cost base that is currently amplifying revenue declines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength four is a deleveraging record and a longer runway. The company's leverage measure fell to 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end from 3.9x and the credit facility was extended to December 2029, which reduces refinancing pressure and shows past willingness to repay debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength five is service content. Services were 26.90% of second-quarter revenue and management expects recurring revenue of 25% to 35%, which stabilises cash flow through the capital cycle if the share rises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness one is operating leverage. Revenue fell 8.6% and adjusted EBITDA 22.2% in the second quarter, so a further volume shortfall cuts earnings faster than revenue and pushes leverage and interest cover toward weaker levels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness two is dependence on add-backs. The CAD 103.3 million gap between adjusted and reported EBITDA is 27.11% of adjusted EBITDA, so the company's own leverage of 3.1x understates the cash cost of its program for as long as charges recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness three is financial policy while leverage is above target. The CAD 61.3 million of repurchases in the second quarter used cash that could have reduced net debt, and the filings give no restricted payment limit that would stop repeat repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness four is reporting reliability. An unremediated material weakness in internal control, an interim finance chief and a new chief executive raise the chance that adjusted measures or accruals are later revised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness five is cash flow volatility. Free cash flow moved from a CAD 52.3 million outflow in fiscal 2025 to an inflow of CAD 371.7 million in fiscal 2026 as the company states it, on working capital and a settlement, and the first half of fiscal 2027 produced only CAD 36.5 million, so debt service cannot be assumed from a single year's figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nine-dimension profile is assessed from the evidence above. Scale and market position is average: revenue of CAD 2,867.2 million over the last twelve months across several end markets, but no market share data. Competitive advantage is average, resting mainly on management statements about differentiated technology. Business diversification is average: four end markets, but life sciences is 51.43% of first-half revenue and customer concentration is not quantified. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital expenditure is low and guided to CAD 60 million to CAD 80 million, yet the fixed-cost base is large enough to need a multi-year reduction program. Margin stability is weak because a revenue decline of 8.6% produced an adjusted EBITDA decline of 22.2%. Free cash flow stability is average: conversion is high but swings with working capital and one-off collections. Ability to refinance is average, helped by the extended facility and a first large maturity in December 2028, and limited by leverage above target. Liquidity position is strong. Financial policy and governance is average: deleveraging in fiscal 2026 is offset by repurchases above target and a control weakness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ATS earns about 54% of adjusted revenue from construction contracts, which are project-timed and discretionary for customers, and about a quarter from services, which are steadier. Customers are primarily large multinationals, and customer concentration is named as a risk but not quantified, so revenue durability is average rather than strong. The order book converts to revenue over several quarters and includes long-duration enterprise programs in life sciences, which explains why revenue lags bookings in both directions; this makes the third-quarter guide, not the second-quarter bookings, the better indicator of near-term cash. Sales into the U.S. from Canadian and European operations are just over 20% of adjusted revenue and exposed to tariffs and the exchange rate, although management says tariff changes at the end of October remove the effect on most covered products.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 29; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 12; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is public with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so there is neither sponsor support nor sponsor extraction to evidence; the debt sits with the listed company, guaranteed by subsidiaries that are borrowers or guarantors under the credit facility, whose names are not listed. Financial policy is therefore a board and management matter, set out in a leverage target range of 2.0x to 3.0x that management has said it will exceed through fiscal 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are exposed to operating leverage. In the second quarter gross margin fell to 28.5% from 29.9% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.1% from 14.2% on lower volumes and mix, while selling, general and administrative costs fell less than revenue. The program targets about CAD 65 million to CAD 75 million of annualised savings, with payback under a year, but lower revenues and mix are temporarily offsetting its benefits, so margins are more likely to defend through cost action than through volume in the next two quarters. The sensitivity to volume is the central credit risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is supported by low capital intensity: capital expenditure was about 2.65% of last-twelve-months revenue and is guided lower, and free cash flow equalled 0.93x reported EBITDA. Restructuring cash costs, cash taxes and lease principal sit on top, and working capital was close to neutral in the first half of fiscal 2027, which produced only CAD 36.5 million of free cash flow after restructuring and a CAD 25.8 million tax payment, so durable cash available for debt service is lower than conversion implies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Industry forces matter for credit mainly through buyer power and cycle timing. Buyers are large and decide timing of capital projects, so orders swing and revenue follows with a lag; supplier power is limited, as supplier lead times are generally acceptable and supply chain effects of trade changes have been largely mitigated through alternative sourcing and pricing. Evidence on rivalry, new entrants and substitutes beyond management's claim of differentiated technology is not in the supplied files, so those forces are not assessed. Political and trade factors are material: the USMCA review process and Section 338 tariffs delayed packaging orders in the second quarter. Exchange-rate factors also matter because the Canadian operations earn significant U.S. dollar revenue that exceeds the natural hedge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit-translated, strengths are scale across end markets, backlog, service content and a funded cost program; weaknesses are operating leverage, add-back dependence, repurchases above target and reporting reliability; opportunities are nuclear and radiopharmaceutical demand and tariff relief; threats are customer deferrals, further tariff changes and a failure to deliver savings on the stated timetable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the near-term outlook is for lower revenue, with third-quarter revenue guided below the prior year and earlier goals for growth and margin expansion no longer expected, and benefits from the program accruing over about 15 months. Over three to five years management points to nuclear refurbishment, radiopharmaceuticals and services as growth areas and keeps a 15% adjusted margin target; these support the credit case only if cost savings arrive and leverage returns to range before the 2028 notes mature.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside path starts with a further delay in non-life-sciences orders, for example if tariff uncertainty persists, so that third-quarter revenue lands below the guided range. The first operational break is fixed costs: in the second quarter an 8.6% revenue decline produced a 22.2% fall in adjusted EBITDA. As an analyst illustration anchored on the 15.54% first-half fall in adjusted EBITDA, applying that fall to last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of CAD 277.8 million gives about CAD 234.63 million, which lifts net leverage to 4.46x, or 4.15x pro forma for the facility sale, and lowers cash interest cover to 2.57x. Liquidity would still hold: the company would have cash of about CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn, although the revolver depends on covenant tests whose levels are not supplied. The consequence for refinancing is that the notes due in December 2028 would need to be refinanced with leverage above the target range, so a lender would look for restructuring savings to be visible in reported EBITDA first. Management levers are to stop repurchases, cut capital expenditure toward the bottom of the CAD 60 million to CAD 80 million range, accelerate the program and use the facility sale proceeds. The observable triggers are third-quarter revenue below CAD 640 million, the leverage measure above 3.1x, and any covenant disclosure. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in this illustration, but not to hold leverage in its target range.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, ATS presents an adequate business profile supported by scale across end markets, a life-sciences-led backlog and ample liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that fall faster than revenue, adjusted measures that rely on large add-backs, leverage above target and a financial policy that still includes repurchases. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but volatile because fiscal 2026 conversion rested on working capital and a one-off collection. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage returning to the 2.0x to 3.0x range and on the restructuring savings appearing in reported EBITDA before the December 2028 notes. The primary downside path is a further order delay that cuts revenue below the guided range while fixed costs and add-backs persist. Further analysis would require covenant levels, the ranking and security of the notes, restricted payment limits and the audited annual notes. Fundamental credit view completed. Top risk: reported EBITDA falling faster than restructuring savings arrive while leverage is above target.
